We track the particle velocity as it accelerates from rest toward its terminal drift value. The field strength, charge, and drag coefficient set the approach. The velocity relaxes smoothly to a steady drift.

Classical/known terms: qE (driving force), -bv (Stokes linear drag), and division by m. The quadratic drag term -c_quad*v*Abs(v) is a standard nonlinear drag form also found in textbooks. Beyond these, the equation introduces several nontrivial composite terms: (1) a saturating driving-force reduction -qE*beta_field*v/(v_ref+Abs(v)), representing field saturation with drift velocity; (2) a coupling to a dynamically evolving screening charge q_eff via -alpha_screen*q_eff, where q_eff itself follows a relaxation-plus-shear-stripping ODE (q0_screen - q_eff)/tau_screen - kappa_shear*Abs(v)*q_eff; and (3) a coupling to a lagging polarization displacement p_pol via -gamma_pol*p_pol, where p_pol follows a relaxation ODE toward a velocity-driven, nonlinearly saturating target chi_pol*v/(1+nl_pol*Abs(v)/v_pol). While each individual physical concept (electrophoretic relaxation, ionic cloud polarization, screening-charge dynamics) has grounding in colloid/electrophoresis physics, the specific composite closed three-state ODE system with these exact functional forms — velocity-dependent shear stripping of screening charge, saturating polarization response, and the particular saturating field term — is not a standard textbook formula. No existing reference presents this exact combined form, and an LLM could not recite it verbatim from background knowledge; the specific coupling structures and saturation forms could only be identified through data-driven inference. Thus, relative to the classical baseline, the equation introduces genuinely novel composite mechanism terms.
